questions.q: What happens if an Apex test method tries to make a real HTTP callout without a mock registered?
options: The callout succeeds normally, identical to production
The test automatically pauses until the real endpoint responds
A CalloutException is thrown
Apex silently skips the callout and returns null
questions.explain: Apex blocks real outbound callouts from test methods; attempting one without Test.setMock registering a mock throws a CalloutException.

questions.q: Which interface must a mock class implement to fake an HTTP callout response in a test?
options: Callable
Queueable
Database.Batchable
HttpCalloutMock
questions.explain: A mock class implements HttpCalloutMock, providing a respond(HttpRequest req) method that returns the fake HttpResponse.

questions.q: What method registers a mock so that a callout made during a test is intercepted and answered by the mock?
options: Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, mockInstance)
Test.startTest()
System.runAs(mockInstance)
Database.insert(mockInstance)
questions.explain: Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, mockInstance) registers the mock instance so any callout made afterward in that test is routed to it instead of a real network call.

questions.q: Why is it important to write a test using a mock that returns a 503 or 500 status, in addition to a test using a 200 success mock?
options: It isn't important — only the success case needs testing
A 503 response automatically increases code coverage more than a 200 response
It proves the code's error-handling path works correctly when the external system fails, not just its happy path
Apex requires at least one failure-status mock per test class to compile
questions.explain: Testing a failure response is negative-path testing applied to integration code — it proves your code surfaces or handles an external failure gracefully instead of assuming the external system always succeeds.

questions.q: What does StaticResourceCalloutMock provide that a hand-written HttpCalloutMock implementation does not inherently give you?
options: The ability to skip Test.setMock entirely
A built-in way to load the mocked response body from an uploaded Static Resource instead of hardcoding it as a string in Apex
Automatic retries on callout failure
Bypassing the need for the HttpCalloutMock interface
questions.explain: StaticResourceCalloutMock is a built-in mock that loads its response body from a Static Resource you upload, which can be more convenient than hardcoding a large JSON or XML string directly in Apex.
